articles.title: Katy Perry Told Her Therapist She Wanted a ‘Legendary Love.’ Then She Met Justin Trudeau: ‘Missing Puzzle Piece’ (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Perry and Trudeau were first linked in July 2025. Now their romance has the superstar talking in lyrics
articles.body:
Katy Perry opens up to PEOPLE about touring through heartbreak and finding love with Justin Trudeau

"I'm living my f---ing life to the fullest!" she says

The pop superstar's concert film, Katy Perry: The Lifetimes Tour - Live from Paris hits theaters and IMAX on Wednesday, Sept. 2

Katy Perry is in a bathing suit, still drying off from a dip in the pool with her 6-year-old daughter Daisy , when she answers a video call on her phone. The pop superstar is finally relishing some downtime 16 months after she hit the road for her hit Lifetimes Tour , with Daisy along for the ride.

"She's seeing her mother in her purpose, and that's good for her; she sees her mom being strong. But also, not every day was easy," says Perry, 41. "Look, last year was really hard." Indeed, the tour came during a transitional period for Perry, who — after facing a harsh reception for her most recent album 143 — weathered a public breakup last summer from Daisy's dad and her partner of nearly 10 years, Orlando Bloom.

Despite the tumult, the "Teenage Dream" singer continued to shine and own the night onstage. "I learned how to step back into my purpose," she says, "and I got the greatest gift from this tour: I got to meet the love of my life." That would be Justin Trudeau , 54, the former Canadian prime minister, whom she met while on the road .

A year later the singer is happier than ever and looking back on the momentous sojourn with her concert film, Katy Perry: The Lifetimes Tour—Live From Paris (in theaters and IMAX for a limited time Wednesday, Sept. 2).

"A lot of people said I couldn't do it and gave me a lot of flak — and I did it. Some people are like, 'Cringe, cringe, cringe,' " she says. "But I'm living my f---ing life to the fullest!"

Perry kicked off the tour in April 2025, just months before reps for her and former fiancé Bloom confirmed their split . She was in Australia when the news broke in July. "It was probably the hardest time. My friends were all hanging out back home. I was crying and just feeling far away," Perry says of her lowest point. "But then my angels went to work. They really showed up."

By the end of that month, she and Trudeau ignited romance rumors when they stepped out for a dinner date in Montreal and the ex-politician was spotted at her show two days later with his daughter (he has three children from a previous marriage).

"I got to meet Justin on tour, and then things shifted," she says. A firm believer in manifestation, Perry wrote down a list last August. On this call she picks up her phone and pulls a piece of paper out of her case. Unfolding it while holding it up to the camera, she reads the last line item aloud: "No. 10 just says, 'True Love.' And I think that's where we're at."

In October the pair took their relationship public, stepping out for her birthday in Paris — and this June they made their red carpet debut at the Tribeca Festival premiere of the concert film. That same month Perry released "Watch It Burn," a fiery breakup single seemingly inspired by last year's uncoupling.

"I wouldn't have stayed in something for nine years if there wasn't really important things to learn. Each relationship is a teacher, right?" she says. "I had to let it go so I could move forward. I always wanted this epic legendary love , and I was talking to my therapist about it: Everything in my life is epic, but this is kind of the missing puzzle piece — then it showed up."

And Trudeau showed up for her all summer, in the crowd at 10 of her 20 recent shows. "He knows the words, he's supportive, and he's in awe; it's super healing," says Perry, who adds that "he is really heart-centered, and I think that we align in that way. I'm so grateful."

With the tour behind her, Perry surely has more love songs in her future — but for now she's focused on the precious everyday moments.

"[I'm] living my life," she says, "so I can write about my life."

For more on Katy Perry, pick up the new issue of PEOPLE, on newsstands everywhere Friday.

articles.summary: Evento reúne gastronomia, cosplay, artes marciais, música, oficinas, atrações internacionais e experiências do universo geek até o feriado de segunda-feira (7).
articles.body:
Festival da Cultura Japonesa 'Bon Odori' começa nesta sexta (4) em Salvador — Foto: Divulgação Bon Odori

A 18ª edição do Festival da Cultura Japonesa de Salvador Bon Odori começa nesta sexta-feira (4), a partir das 10h, no Parque de Exposições de Salvador. A programação segue até a segunda-feira (7). Os ingressos custam a partir de R$ 52 (inteira) e R$ 26 (meia) e podem ser adquiridos no site do evento .

Pela primeira vez em sua história, o evento terá quatro dias consecutivos de atividades. Com a programação estendida, o festival está com atrações diversificadas como música, dança, apresentações de ilusionismo, artes marciais, desfiles de cosplay, oficinas, exposições, gastronomia japonesa e atividades ligadas ao universo geek, dos games e dos animes.

Os ingressos também podem podem ser adquiridos na bilheteria do Parque de Exposições durante os quatro dias de evento. Há a opção de ingresso social para qualquer pessoa mediante a entrega de 1 kg de alimento não perecível na entrada do festival.

Neste ano, os convidados especiais são Bianca Alencar, atriz, dubladora e conhecida por dar voz a personagens como Mabel Pines, de Gravity Falls, Twilight Sparkle, de My Little Pony, e Pinky Dinky Doo, da série homônima. E Henrique Marangon, o Core, criador de conteúdo conhecido por transformar mistérios e curiosidades do universo dos games em investigações que unem pesquisa, entretenimento e criatividade.

Além dos brasileiros, a cantora japonesa Nanase Aikawa, destaque do J-rock dos anos 1990, estará presente no evento. A artista participa de atividades especiais durante o festival.

Toda a arrecadação no Bon Odori será destinada ao programa Bahia Sem Fome, por meio da Secretaria da Agricultura, Pecuária, Irrigação, Pesca e Aquicultura do Estado da Bahia. Também é possível comprar os ingressos antecipadamente nas lojas da Ticket Maker localizadas no Shopping da Bahia, Shopping Paralela e Parque Shopping Bahia.

O público que optar por ir de carro ou moto terá acesso com estacionamento no Parque de Exposições, com venda realizada exclusivamente no local. O acesso aos estacionamentos poderá ser feito tanto pela Av. Luís Viana Filho – Paralela quanto pela Av. Dorival Caymmi – Itapuã.

articles.title: Rock in Rio: 190 shows e 7 dias de festival na Cidade do Rock | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival começa nesta sexta-feira (4), na Cidade do Rock. Programação vai receber 190 apresentações e cerca de 1,3 mil artistas.
articles.summary: O Rock in Rio inicia nesta sexta-feira uma maratona de 91 horas de música com 190 apresentações e 1,3 mil artistas espalhados pela Cidade do Rock.
articles.body:
O Rock in Rio começa sua nova edição, nesta sexta-feira (4), com uma programação extensa e números que impressionam. Ao longo de sete dias de festival, a Cidade do Rock, na Zona Oeste do Rio, vai receber 190 apresentações e cerca de 1,3 mil artistas, em uma área de 385 mil metros quadrados.

Ao todo, serão 91 horas de programação, distribuídas em sete palcos e diferentes espaços de entretenimento.

No palco Mundo, o principal do festival, estão nomes como Elton John, Foo Fighters, Maroon 5, Stray Kids e Twenty One Pilots. O grupo de K-pop Stray Kids faz sua estreia no Rock in Rio.

A programação também inclui espaços voltados a diferentes estilos musicais. O New Dance Order é dedicado à música eletrônica, enquanto o Espaço Favela reúne ritmos como samba e funk. Já o Supernova é voltado a novos talentos e o Sunset ficou conhecido pelos encontros entre grandes artistas.

Para Roberta Medina, vice-presidente do festival, a diversidade está no DNA do Rock in Rio desde a primeira edição.

“A diversidade está no DNA do Rock in Rio. Ele nunca poderia ter nascido com essa dimensão, com a magnitude, com alcance mundial que ele teve se ele não tivesse atingido já desde a primeira edição vários estilos musicais, vários públicos diferentes”, afirmou.

Cidade do Rock — Foto: Thaís Espírito Santo/g1 Rio

Quem vai à Cidade do Rock também encontra brinquedos e experiências imersivas. Entre as atrações estão a montanha-russa, o Discovery e outros brinquedos que fazem parte da estrutura do festival.

Nesta edição, o público também pode acompanhar uma experiência sensorial de luz e som. O espetáculo Ecco utiliza tecnologia audiovisual e chega pela primeira vez à arena da Cidade do Rock.

A programação ainda inclui o Global Village, espaço que reúne referências arquitetônicas e culturais de diferentes partes do mundo.

A cenografia reproduz elementos inspirados em lugares como o Taj Mahal, na Índia, e o Teatro Municipal do Rio, além de referências à obra do arquiteto espanhol Gaudí. A proposta é reunir diferentes culturas e públicos em um mesmo espaço, tendo a música como elemento de conexão.

articles.title: Hugo, da dupla com Guilherme, vai a jogo que garantiu acesso à Série C | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor, que nasceu em Morrinhos, mas passou a infância em Goiatuba, acompanhou de perto a partida que garantiu o acesso do Azulão.
articles.summary: Cantor, que nasceu em Morrinhos, mas passou a infância em Goiatuba, acompanhou de perto a partida que garantiu o acesso do Azulão.
articles.body:
O cantor Hugo, da dupla com Guilherme, acompanhou de perto a partida que garantiu o acesso do Goiatuba à Série C do Campeonato Brasileiro de 2027. A presença do cantor começou mesmo antes do jogo rolar.

Hugo esteve próximo dos jogadores e acompanhou a preparação para o jogo, entrou no vestiário, no campo e gritou o gol da classificação da equipe. A relação com Goiatuba vem desde a infância.

O Goiatuba precisava apenas de um empate contra o São José para garantir a classificação. O jogo aconteceu no Estádio Divino Garcia Rosa e terminou em 1 a 1, com o Azulão conquistando o acesso.

A partida começou difícil para o time goiano que saiu perdendo ainda no primeiro tempo. O Goiatuba pressionou em busca do empate e conseguiu chegar ao gol aos 36 minutos da segunda etapa após um gol contra do atleta do São José.

Com o empate, o Goiatuba garantiu o acesso à Série C e iniciou a festa no estádio. Embora tenha nascido em Morrinhos, o cantor cresceu na cidade e mantém uma ligação afetiva com o município.

articles.body:
Cachaça — Foto: Luiz Gabriel Franco / g1

A 1ª edição do Festival da Cachaça acontece de 11 a 13 de setembro em Ribeirão Preto (SP). O evento reúne expositores de cachaças artesanais, música sertaneja, manifestações da cultura caipira e gastronomia. A entrada é gratuita.

Segundo a organização, o público pode conversar diretamente com produtores e ter experiências ligadas à bebida. Estão confirmados participantes de cidades paulistas como Serrana, Mococa, São Simão, Batatais, Sales Oliveira, Itu, Torre de Pedra, Jaboticabal, Ourinhos, Ribeirão Preto, Rio Claro, Itupeva e Capão Bonito.

Produtores de queijos, charcutaria, cafés especiais, antepastos e diferentes tipos de artesanato participam do festival. Os visitantes poderão adquirir os itens durante o evento.

Além da bebida como protagonista, a programação prevê apresentações musicais e manifestações populares.

A abertura, na sexta-feira (11), conta com a apresentação do berranteiro Aurino. Na sequência, o público acompanha duas apresentações da Orquestra de Violeiros de São Carlos, além da participação do locutor JC Caipirão, também responsável por momentos de locução e discotecagem ao longo da noite.

No sábado (12), a programação reúne música country, sertanejo e manifestações tradicionais. Estão previstas apresentações da banda country Suzie Kill, do Grupo de Catira Espora de Prata, de Barretos (SP), da cantora Daiane Ken e da dupla Zé Simões & Luiz Magner.

Para encerrar o festival, no domingo (13), sobem ao palco as duplas Cleiton Viola & Willian e Neto & Matheus. A programação tem ainda o cantor Ricardo Minelli.

articles.title: Edifício Copan reabre visitas à cobertura com vista panorâmica do Centro de SP por R$ 50 | G1
articles.standfirst: Passeios guiados ao terraço voltam neste sábado (5); renda será destinada à restauração da fachada do edifício projetado por Oscar Niemeyer.
articles.summary: Passeios guiados ao terraço voltam neste sábado (5); renda será destinada à restauração da fachada do edifício projetado por Oscar Niemeyer.
articles.body:
O edifício Copan vai reabrir neste sábado (5) as visitas guiadas à sua cobertura, que tem vista panorâmica para o Centro de São Paulo . O passeio vai custar R$ 50 por pessoa, e o dinheiro será usado para custear a restauração da fachada do prédio, que está coberta por uma tela de proteção há 15 anos.

Com duração aproximada de 40 minutos, as visitas acontecerão sempre aos sábados, das 13h30 às 16h30, em grupos de até oito pessoas – limite de capacidade do elevador original do edifício. Os ingressos com agendamento de horário serão vendidos em um site próprio .

Do alto do mirante, a 115 metros do solo, é possível observar pontos turísticos próximos, como a Catedral da Sé, ou distantes, como o Pico do Jaraguá. O único obstáculo à vista é o vizinho Edifício Itália, alguns metros mais alto do que o Copan.

De acordo com o síndico, Guilherme Milani, os recursos extras serão importantes para viabilizar a recuperação da fachada norte do edifício, voltada à Avenida Ipiranga. Ela reúne cerca de 46 mil metros quadrados de pastilhas e teve o custo da restauração estimado em R$ 68 milhões em 2023. A expectativa do condomínio é iniciar as obras até dezembro de 2027.

A retomada das visitas (interrompidas seis anos atrás e antes gratuitas) faz parte de uma estratégia da administração para ampliar as receitas do condomínio a partir de sua vocação turística e cultural. Além dos passeios, estão em estudo novas fontes de arrecadação, como exploração de mídia indoor, locação do foyer para eventos e a criação de uma área do terraço destinada a locações.

Inaugurado em 1966, o Copan é uma das obras mais famosas do arquiteto Oscar Niemeyer e um dos principais cartões postais da cidade. O edifício de fachada curva tem 115 metros de altura, 1.160 apartamentos e cerca de 3 mil moradores.

Vista do Centro à Zona Norte de São Paulo a partir do terraço do Edifício Copan — Foto: Leonardo Zvarick/g1

Ao longo das décadas, o prédio acompanhou as transformações do Centro da capital. Depois de enfrentar um longo período de degradação e esvaziamento da região, nos últimos anos voltou a atrair turistas, produções audiovisuais, eventos culturais e visitantes interessados na arquitetura modernista.

Segundo informações divulgadas pela administração, o edifício recebe atualmente cerca de 35 mil hóspedes por ano em apartamentos de temporada e mantém todas as suas 72 lojas ocupadas.

Devido a sua importância cultural, desde 2012 o Copan é tombado pelo Conselho Municipal de Preservação do Patrimônio Histórico, Cultural e Ambiental da Cidade de São Paulo (Conpresp).

📅 Quando? Todo sábado, a partir de 5/9; das 13h30 às 16h30

O Capital Inicial ensaiou na tarde desta quinta-feira (03) para o show do Rock in Rio. Ao som de "Independência", Dinho Ouro Preto falava com os funcionários que estavam na Cidade do Rock, no Rio de Janeiro, trabalhando no evento.

articles.title: Vicente Vallés reflexiona sobre la “pregunta” qué debería hacerse Pedro Sánchez tras el “ataque” a Ceuta: “No queremos hacer nada con Marruecos”
articles.standfirst: El presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’ habla del presidente del Gobierno en ‘La Mesa’
articles.summary: El presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’ habla del presidente del Gobierno en ‘La Mesa’
articles.body: Cristina Pardo ha estrenado este miércoles, 2 de septiembre, su nuevo formato en Antena 3. En ‘La Mesa’ se han reunido Iván Redondo, Carlos Alsina y Vicente Vallés. Este último ha reflexionado sobre la pregunta que debería hacerse Pedro Sánchez, especialmente tras sus declaraciones inmediatas tras la entrada irregular de migrantes a las fronteras de Ceuta. Por aquel entonces, el 31 de julio exactamente, el líder del PSOE afirmó que se había producido un “ataque a la integridad territorial de España”. Aunque Vallés comprende que “gobernar es muy difícil”, no entiende el giro radical que ha tomado parte del Ejecutivo alrededor de esta crisis. “Una parte especialmente difícil de gobernar es la parte diplomática y todavía más difícil es gestionar a Marruecos en esa parte diplomática. Eso es perfectamente comprensible”, apunta el presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’, quien reconoce además que él mismo es “comprensivo” con la labor del presidente del Gobierno. Ahora bien, este cambio de paradigma se escapa de su control. Por eso, señala que Pedro Sánchez debería hacerse una pregunta: “¿Quién ha sido el atacante?”. Esta sería la cuestión principal que debería rondar la cabeza del líder del Ejecutivo, según Vallés, ya que “si ponemos el dedo en quién ha sido el atacante, el Gobierno tiene la responsabilidad de hacer algo con respecto a ese atacante”. No obstante, la impresión del periodista es completamente opuesta a lo que, a su juicio, debería hacer el Gobierno. “Como no queremos hacer nada con respecto a Marruecos, no queremos situar el dedo como atacante a Marruecos”, sentencia Vallés. Esta forma de explicar la situación ha sido muy compartida en redes sociales, con muchos usuarios mostrándose de acuerdo con las palabras del presentador de ‘Antena 3 Noticias’.

articles.title: Carla Jeffery, star of Disney's 'Zombies' movies, dies at 33
articles.summary: The actor's costars paid tribute to "the sweetest, kindest, most loving person."
articles.body:
Carla Jeffery, an actor best known for her role in Disney's Zombies franchise, has died at 33.

Her cause of death was not immediately available.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the passing of our beloved Carla Jeffery," her manager, Carla Alexander, said in a statement posted to Jeffery's Instagram. "Carla joined the Alexanders Talent Management family at the age of 12. For more than 20 years, we had the privilege of watching her grow into a beautiful, vibrant, and incredibly talented woman whose radiant smile could light up any room.

"As Bree in Disney's hit Zombies franchise, Carla shared her joy, humor, and bright spirit with audiences around the world. Carla was more than a client; she was family.

"Our hearts are with Carla's family and loved ones during this devastating time. We respectfully ask that their privacy be honored as they grieve this unimaginable loss."

Jeffery played cheerleader Bree Prattle in Disney's three Zombies movies between 2018 and 2022, and voiced the character in 2024's TV show Zombies: The Re-Animated Series .

The actor's Zombies castmates have paid tribute to her. Chandler Kinney remembered Jeffery as "the sweetest, most sparkly gal." She wrote on Instagram , "This doesn't feel real. You made every day better and brighter with your infectious positivity."

Milo Manheim wrote, "Love you Carlaboo, the sweetest, kindest, most loving person."

Trevor Tordjman wrote, "Carla, you will be missed. Will never forget your energy. Truly one of a kind."

Erika Ishii wrote, "This is absolutely heartbreaking. We only got to meet in person just once in the booth, but she was incredibly sweet and kind and we were both giddy over getting to record at Disney. Deepest condolences to her family and friends."

In a statement, Disney Entertainment Television said: "Carla Jeffery's extraordinary talent, warmth and spirit left an indelible mark on everyone who had the privilege of working with her. She had a rare gift for connecting with audiences, and her performances brought joy to millions.

"We will remember Carla for her generosity, her humor and the genuine light she brought to those around her. We offer our deepest condolences to her family and loved ones, her castmates and collaborators, and the countless fans whose lives she touched."

Jeffery made her acting debut in 2006's romantic comedy Phat Girlz. She also appeared in shows including Curb Your Enthusiasm , the Nickelodeon sitcom iCarly and Disney Channel's Shake It Up .

She had previously spoken out about having epilepsy, which she said she initially did not want to talk to her colleagues or manager about.

"When I first got into acting, I was not comfortable talking about my epilepsy," Jeffery told the Epilepsy Foundation in 2022 , having opened up about her condition after suffering a seizure on the set of Zombies.

"I was worried that I would have a seizure while reading lines or on set. I was even scared to tell my manager for fear that she wouldn't send me on any auditions. But, on the contrary, once I told her, she encouraged me to not let it hold me back. It helped me realize there was more to me than just my epilepsy."

She added: "I want everyone to know not to be scared of who you are. I've had this for years, and it's not going anywhere. I just have to work around it. I'm going to keep doing what I love, and at the same time, use my story to help others. I want to be an inspiration."

No cause of death has been confirmed as yet and there has been no indication that the death was linked to Jeffery's epilepsy.

She was the twin sister of fellow actor Carlon Jeffery, who appeared in Disney Channel's A.N.T. Farm .

articles.title: Miley Cyrus Drops Last Name, Prompting Dad Billy Ray to Publicly Defend the Change: ‘Family Means More Than Ever Now’
articles.summary: Miley Cyrus has dropped her last name in the lead up to her tenth studio album, “Bass Persuades,” prompting her father, Billy Ray Cyrus, to speak out on X in...
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus has dropped her last name in the lead up to her tenth studio album, "Bass Persuades," prompting her father, Billy Ray Cyrus, to speak out on X in defense of the decision.

Miley's announcement fueled the rumor mill about alleged ongoing tensions between the pop star and her father (see The Daily Beast headline: "Pop Star Rebukes Dad With Plan to Change Her Famous Name"). But according to Billy Ray, Miley notified him about the name change in advance and he had nothing but support for his Grammy-winning daughter.

"Family means more than ever now," Billy Ray Cyrus wrote on X. "I always called my little girl Miley. Just … Miley. Just like I always called my little boy Braison. Bet you didn't know … I was just CYRUS before Achy Breaky Heart came out in 92…. I told Miley yesterday I felt good about her going with her first name. I mentioned Dolly and Cher. Thinking about it more and more … Elvis .. Prince … and so on. It's a natural progression for an iconic superstar legend. And the legend continues ! Looking forward to the new album."

Miley Cyrus announced Sept. 1 that her new album is titled "Bass Persuades" and will release on September 18 via Atlantic Records. The tracklist for the album includes 10 songs, plus features from Model/Actriz and Miike Snow's Andrew Wyatt. Cyrus will promote the album with a rare return to the stage courtesy of a two-night stint at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles on Oct. 16 and 18.

"Music takes hold of us. We feel it, sing it, sometimes dance to it, let it out and carry on. It is powerful, vulnerable, sweet and strong," Miley wrote in announcing the album. "Heart full, heartache, every part of life in between. That's what the title means to me. Thank you for being a part of making my wildest dreams come true. I sincerely hope you love this album."

While rumors have persisted for years about tensions between Miley Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus, the duo reunited earlier this year on the "Hannah Montana" 20th anniversary special. Miley told People at the time that music is how the two have always stayed bonded, even amid family hardships.

"It's really the way we communicate," Miley said. "Whether it's sending a song we wrote in a text or writing a poem that says how we feel in a way that's authentic to us, it's always been the way we share our feelings."

articles.title: The best red carpet looks from the 2026 Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: The Venice Film Festival, which typically sees the glamour of Hollywood travel by boat to the island of Lido every September, has arrived. This year, the 10-day red carpet roll-out will host the likes of Robert Pattinson, George and Amal Clooney and Penélope Cruz.
articles.body: The Venice Film Festival, which typically sees Hollywood A-listers travel by boat to the little island of Lido every September, has arrived. This year, the 10-day red carpet event will host the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Penélope Cruz, Robert Pattinson and Patrick Schwarzenegger and more in their formal finest. Some films will be watched too. The festival has long been a glamorous affair, but it has recently become a major platform for fashion news, fueling the industry marketing machine: Last year, Julia Roberts lent Amanda Seyfried her Dario Vitale Versace suit, Ayo Edibiri made her Venice debut in a custom red strapless dress by Chanel that teased Matthieu Blazy’s new direction, and Greta Lee did the same for Jonathan Anderson’s Dior. The event has come to be seen as an early finger in the wind ahead of the Oscars. This year, the movies in the running for the Golden Lion prize are deep, dark and, politically charged. Danny Boyle’s “Ink” – an adaptation of the acclaimed play about the early years of Rupert Murdoch (Guy Pearce) and his acquisition of London tabloid paper “The Sun” – kicks off the festival on its opening night. Following will be Werner Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” with sisters Kate and Rooney Mara who fall in love with the same man (Orlando Bloom), and Florian Zeller’s “Bunker,” in which real-life partners Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem play a couple whose marriage becomes strained after the husband agrees to build a survivalist bunker for a tech billionaire. However, the lineup has already drawn criticism for its lack of female directors — this year just two films, May el-Toukhy’s “Woman Unknown” and Rachel Szor’s “NAZA,” directed by women are in the main competition for the grand prize. “There’s a systemic problem. It’s much harder for women to get their films financed,” said director Maggie Gyllenhaal, the jury president for this year’s festival. “Who decides what’s good and valuable?” Gyllenhaal is also screening a short Marilyn Monroe biopic starring Dakota Johnson and Ellen Burstyn, though it’s not competing. With just a handful of Hollywood stars set to grace the carpet, there’s reason to believe the fashion on show might skew considered and cerebral. But with musicians like Phoebe Bridgers as well as Liam and Noel Gallagher expected to make an appearance — the Gallagher brothers are rarely seen on a red carpet, let alone together — there’s still plenty to look forward to. articles.title: Jennifer Aniston’s boyfriend Jim Curtis opens up on partial paralysis, chronic nerve damage which makes him walk with a limp now: ‘You don't have to live as a victim'
articles.summary: Jennifer Aniston has been in a relationship with life coach and hypnotist Jim Curtis since 2025, and the couple has gradually become more open about t.
articles.body: Jennifer Aniston has been in a relationship with life coach and hypnotist Jim Curtis since 2025, and the couple has gradually become more open about their life together. Curtis, 50, is also an author and has recently released a book titled 'The Book of Possibility'. In a rare appearance with Aniston, he spoke candidly about a deeply personal chapter of his life, being diagnosed with lesions on his spinal cord in his 20s, a condition that resulted in chronic nerve damage and partial paralysis.Aniston, 57, and Curtis made a rare joint appearance at the 92nd Street Y in New York City on Wednesday, September 2, where they attended an event celebrating Curtis’ new book. During the conversation, Curtis reflected on how his health struggles changed the way he viewed himself, his body and his life.Curtis, who now walks with a limp, described the diagnosis as an ultimate low. Recalling the night he first learned about his condition, he said he had been experiencing severe pain and spent hours in a New York City emergency room.As quoted by People, “I found myself in the hospital one night because I was having such severe pain in my body, and in a New York City emergency room, I was there for 13 hours, and it was maybe 2:00 am. and the nurse came, and I said, ‘Is the doctor going to see me? What are you working me up for?’ And she said, ‘A diagnosis right there,’” Curtis recounted. “And it was a really scary diagnosis.”Curtis said that looking up the diagnosis on Google while still in the hospital made the situation even more frightening. He recalled feeling his body “freeze and seize up without the fear of what Google had to say about this.”Despite the fear, he eventually tried to shift his mindset and tell himself, “Tomorrow, everything changes.” Curtis explained that learning to approach his condition differently was not an overnight process and required years of personal growth.“I’m not saying here that the doctor tells you to do something you should get up and leave,” Curtis said. “What I’m saying is that you don’t have to live as the victim. You don’t have to live in your suffering.”He further explained that accepting one's struggles can eventually change the way they are experienced.Curtis said those struggles “can become your power as soon as you accept and love them”However, getting to that point of acceptance was difficult for him. Curtis admitted that he was once embarrassed about his medical condition and would give people a different explanation for his injury.“I would say I got into a motorcycle accident,” Curtis said. “I was so shameful that I had a medical condition. [I thought] I was broken in some way. I thought the motorcycle accident was at least a little macho.”Curtis said that he eventually managed to “overcome” those feelings through “self-acceptance and self-love”, although he believes the process could have been shorter.The discussion also turned towards life choices and finding one's purpose. Aniston, who rarely speaks publicly about her relationship with Curtis, asked him a question about helping someone who feels trapped in an unfulfilling life.“If someone said to you, ‘I’m at this crossroads, and I am stuck, and I’m in this rat race of a life, and I’m fully invested, but I know that’s not my calling. My soul, my heart is screaming to do something else’. How would you help coach someone through that?”Curtis explained that he does not advise people to abruptly abandon their existing responsibilities in pursuit of a dream.“I’m not a proponent of ‘drop everything and leave,’” he replied. “That [acceptance] was 25 years in the making for me.”“There’s a reality of life too. You have rent to pay and medical bills to pay and kids to feed, all of your stuff,” he continued. “But I will say this: you don’t have to let fear stop you from living your dream. You can manifest at any time by placing your focus on the outcomes that you want.”More about Jennifer Aniston and Jim Curtis’ RelationshipAniston and Curtis were first romantically linked in July 2025. Their relationship has since attracted considerable attention, although the two have largely kept their personal lives away from the spotlight.In May, Curtis shared several pictures featuring Aniston, including a kissing selfie, while PEOPLE subsequently confirmed that the couple had celebrated their first anniversary. Curtis has also spoken about becoming part of Aniston’s close-knit circle of friends. During an appearance on The Jamie Kern Lima Show on August 31, he discussed the strong bond Aniston shares with her longtime friends, including fellow Friends star Courteney Cox. He described the group as “like family” and added, “I feel incredibly blessed to be part [of] and welcomed into that family.”Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Arrest warrant issued for ‘Below Deck Mediterranean’ star Nathan Gallagher
articles.summary: Australian police have issued an arrest warrant for “Below Deck Mediterranean” star Nathan Gallagher after he missed a court appearance related to an alleged domestic violence incident.
articles.body: Australian police have issued an arrest warrant for “Below Deck Mediterranean” star Nathan Gallagher after he missed a court appearance related to an alleged domestic violence incident. New South Wales police shared a photo of Gallagher, 28, and asked the public for help locating him. He is known to frequent the Emington and Melrose Park areas but is “believed to be offshore,” authorities said in a news release, which notes he has outstanding warrants in Sydney. In a Facebook post, police warned the public not to approach him if spotted. The reality star, from Burtonport, Ireland, works as a deckhand on the Bravo series. He was arrested on domestic violence charges in December 2025, NBC Los Angeles reported. Gallagher was granted conditional bail. He was due back in court Tuesday but never appeared, according to the station. In a statement to Rolling Stone in August, Gallagher acknowledged he has “made mistakes,” but said he didn’t think “the public has heard the full story surrounding what happened.” Police have not named the alleged victim, but Rolling Stone reported that Gallagher’s statement pointed to his former partner and “Below Deck” cast member Gael Cameron. He called the situation “extremely complicated.” “I’m not claiming I was perfect. I wasn’t. I made mistakes and I will take responsibility for my own actions. But I will not accept being portrayed solely through one person’s account of a relationship when there is another side and evidence relating to it,” he told Rolling Stone. Gallagher added his biggest concern was his son, whom he shares with Cameron. “Below Deck Mediterranean” is currently airing its 11th season. Bravo and Cameron did not immediately respond to a request for comment Thursday.

articles.title: 'Deadpool' star Ryan Reynolds torches 1980s nostalgia, calls decade a ‘f---ing mess’ people ‘forget’
articles.summary: Ryan Reynolds called the 1980s a "brutal" and "f---ing mess" at the "Mayday" premiere, sparking fierce pushback from Spencer Pratt and Dan Bongino.
articles.body: Ryan Reynolds faced backlash Thursday after the "Deadpool" star called the 1980s "brutal" and a "f---ing mess" while promoting his Cold-War era movie "Mayday" at its New York premiere, prompting critics to question his characterization of the decade and the contrast with his nostalgia-driven new film. Reynolds said modern nostalgia can obscure the darker realities of distinct periods in history, including the decade depicted in his latest movie. "When you get far enough away from a time period that’s quite distinct, there’s always a lovely feeling associated with it, almost like you pave over all the trauma with puppy dogs and ice cream," Reynolds said in an interview with Variety. "The 80s was a brutal, brutal time for people. It was a f---ing mess and people forget that." RYAN REYNOLDS STARS AS SHOT-DOWN NAVY PILOT RESCUED BY EX-KGB AGENT IN APPLE TV+’S ‘MAYDAY’ Christian Toto, an award-winning film critic and founder of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Reynolds’ comments were especially striking because "Mayday" itself embraces the era Reynolds criticized. "His '80s comments are so stunning. First, he was living in Canada during the 1980s and was pretty young at the time — he's 49 now, meaning in 1986 he was just 9 years of age," he said. "Much more importantly, his new movie 'Mayday' is a love letter to the 1980s. It doesn't describe the decade as perfect, but it's a perfectly sweet nostalgia blast atop a buddy comedy template. Why he would trash the decade, ignoring its joyous spirit and all-American vibe, is a mystery." "Ryan Reynolds is one of the best marketers in Hollywood. And he happens to be an A-list actor, too. His business savvy is unusual, and he personally helped make the 'Deadpool' series a smash via a series of clever comic shorts. He's funny and self-deprecating, too, which never hurts," he added. Lisa Cusack, president of the Don’t L.A. My Burbank PAC and a Los Angeles GOP delegate, told Fox News Digital on Thursday that Reynolds’ criticism overlooked what she viewed as the economic and cultural gains of the Reagan-era 1980s. "Setting aside the fact that anyone could hate on the decade that produced ‘Back to the Future’ and ‘Indiana Jones’, the ‘80s left behind the high inflation and social unrest of the ’70s," she said. "The GDP grew and poverty rates declined. Everyone wanted to move to California and Hollywood was thriving. We don’t want to go back, but the Reagan '80s is actually a pretty good example of how there’s always a way to leave bad ideas behind and make positive progress." HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES Television personality Spencer Pratt, who has publicly advocated for bringing film and television production jobs back to the United States, responded to Reynolds by tying the comments to Hollywood's relationship with American audiences. "Here I am trying to bring back American film jobs, and then these tools keep saying stupid crap like this and making every normal American hate them. Hollywood is seriously its own worst enemy. Just stick to the Cricket wireless ads, dude," Pratt said on X. Fox News Digital reported this week that the U.S. entertainment industry has lost 49,000 jobs since 2022, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data, as productions increasingly shifted to competing states and overseas locations. In Los Angeles, where Pratt recently ran for mayor, scripted television production in the region was down nearly 30% from 2019 and more than 80 production-service businesses had closed since 2022 amid reduced production and industry strikes. TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS Dan Bongino also pushed back on Reynolds’ description of the decade, pointing to the 1980 "Miracle on Ice," the fall of the Berlin Wall, economic growth under former President Ronald Reagan and the era’s popular culture. "This dude doesn’t know jack s--- about the 1980s in America — and Jack left town. I was a teenager when the ’80s ended, and it was an INCREDIBLE time to be alive. No social-media rage farming," Bongino said on X. "The Miracle on Ice kicked off the decade, and the Berlin Wall and communism came crashing down at the end. Reagan putting up monster GDP growth numbers. Pre-woke MTV. ‘Indiana Jones’." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "No men in women’s bathrooms. And much, much more. The ’80s TORE IT UP. Friends don’t let friends fall for Hollywood propaganda. God bless America—and God bless the ’80s!" he added.

articles.title: Eva Shockey says she received 'thousands and thousands' of death threats from anti-hunting activists
articles.summary: Eva Shockey reveals she received thousands and thousands of death threats from anti-hunting activists as her profile grew in the outdoor industry.
articles.body: Eva Shockey says the anti-hunting backlash she faced at the height of her rise in the outdoor industry went far beyond angry comments on social media. It included "thousands and thousands and thousands" of death threats. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Shockey, the daughter of legendary hunter Jim Shockey, opened up about the years of harassment during a recent appearance on the "Country Outdoors" podcast, explaining that she became a frequent target of anti-hunting activists as she gained notoriety. "I was sort of like the poster child for a little while of the anti-hunters and the hatred," Shockey said. The backlash intensified around hunts involving bears and other apex predators, she recalled. And Shockey believes there was a reason critics came after her so aggressively rather than directing the same energy toward her famous father. "I was like the blonde young girl that they thought that they would scare off and could be really mean to and bully, versus my dad, who’s like, ‘I don’t care,’" she said. Shockey also believes much of the outrage came from people who didn’t understand the distinction between legal hunting and illegal poaching. "Still today, people don’t understand what hunting is and poaching," she said. "We hate poachers. That is what I — and we — fight against all the time." JORDAN DAVIS FACES FAN BACKLASH OVER HAWAII AXIS DEER HUNT DESPITE STRONG CONSERVATION BACKING She said she can understand why someone who didn’t grow up around hunting might initially be uncomfortable with it. Her mother, Louise, never hunted herself, despite being married to one of the most famous hunters in the world. "I can appreciate people that are not into it, and I can appreciate their perspective," she said. But she believes media coverage often turns hunting into something entirely different, feeding outrage among people who may not understand wildlife management or conservation. "The media turns it into something where they think they’re doing what’s right by hating it," Shockey said. "But really, when you actually sit down and talk to them, they’re like, ‘Oh, we had no idea.’" OREGON BALLOT MEASURE THAT WOULD HAVE CRIMINALIZED HUNTING AND FISHING FAILS TO QUALIFY FOR VOTE Shockey said her hunting photos were repeatedly used as clickbait before spreading internationally. "It went viral over the UK, and I was on all of their news networks," she said. At the time, Shockey was living in Russia with her now-husband, former NHL player Tim Brandt, who was playing in the Kontinental Hockey League. That was when the harassment reached another level. "There was thousands of death threats — thousands and thousands and thousands — for a really long time," Shockey said. The sheer volume and nature of the threats eventually became difficult to process. Shockey recalled sitting down with her father and trying to make sense of why strangers wanted to harm her over something she viewed as a positive force for conservation, food and outdoor adventure. "This is a lot," she remembered telling him. "There’s death threats coming at me, and they want to do this to me and this to me." To Shockey, the disconnect was baffling. "I’m just out here raising money for conservation and eating whatever we’re hunting and going on adventures and sharing the beautiful creation of God," she said. "How are we getting death threats?" Her father’s response ultimately changed the way she looked at the harassment. "The conversation we had was basically like, you can either get scared and stop and they win, or if you truly believe with your whole heart what you’re doing is right, then why would you be scared?" Shockey said. "Stand up for what you believe in." So she did. Eva Shockey is an advocate for women in the outdoors Not long after that period in her life, Shockey landed on the cover of "Field & Stream." In 2014, she became just the second woman to appear on the iconic outdoor magazine’s cover. The first was Queen Elizabeth II. For Shockey, the significance went far beyond seeing her own face on a magazine she had grown up reading. "It was representing, at the time, so many women that were in the outdoor space, and I got to just be the face of that for that moment," she said. It also carried a more personal meaning after the threats and attempts to intimidate her. Shockey viewed the cover as proof that she wasn’t going anywhere. "It was a really cool representation of, like, we’re not scared because this is what we do," she said. "This is what we believe in." More than a decade later, Shockey remains one of the most recognizable women in hunting. Now a mother of two, she continues to hunt, promote conservation and encourage girls to get involved in the outdoors. That mission has become especially personal given her own experience growing up without female hunters around her. "I just never saw females that hunted," Shockey said. "So I have always loved telling little girls, like, ‘it is so cool. Y’all should try it. Do it. Don’t be scared. Don’t be intimidated.’" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Considering how hard some people once tried to intimidate her, that last part carries a little more weight. articles.title: Former Disney star Dylan Sprouse says acting as a kid was ‘child labor’
articles.summary: Dylan Sprouse called his childhood acting career "child labor" on his "Wildmen" podcast, revealing the mental hurdles he still faces as an adult.
articles.body: Former Disney Channel star Dylan Sprouse is getting candid about how he feels about his career as a child actor. During a recent episode of his podcast, "Wildmen," the 34-year-old actor told his co-host, Brendan Columbus, that he was looking forward to speaking with their guest for that episode, Mark Indelicato, about the demands placed on child actors, calling it "child labor." "I definitely want to dive in and talk with him a little bit about some of that, how he’s coped growing up in the industry because, essentially, we’re beating around the bush, but it’s child labor," Dylan said. "Like, when you work at that age, some kids used to work in coal mines and guard the mine cart door when they were 15, we just sang and danced. It’s still child labor!" He added that he still deals with his own "mental hurdles" when it comes to working in the entertainment industry as an adult, saying he finds it difficult to be "in the same industry I've been in forever." BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA "I act like a kid anyway. So, I wonder if I'm just always chasing that," he said. Sprouse brought the topic of child labor back up when he and Columbus were joined by Indelicato, who starred as Justin Suarez on "Ugly Betty" from ages 12 to 15. Sprouse compared acting as a child to working "a full office job," saying he grew "up in the industry with this kind of workaholic attitude." "I’ve described this to people a lot before – when you’re working on television, it’s a day job," he said. "You go in, you clock in, you clock out, you have a cubicle … it’s different, but it’s the same hours. You work it like that." The two then shot to stardom when they landed the roles of twins Zack and Cody on the Disney Channel show, "The Suite Life of Zack & Cody," and then its spin-off, "The Suite Life on Deck." Following the end of the spin-off, Dylan stepped away from acting, attending Gallatin School of Individualized Study, where he studied video game design. Since graduating in May 2015, Dylan has returned to acting, although he has appeared in projects more sporadically than his brother, and he spoke to Indelicato about feeling like there was a "void" each time a project ended as a kid. "[My father, Matthew Sprouse] desperately wanted us to be normal kids, and my mother wanted us to be a bit more of a caricature of two normal kids," he said on the "Call Her Daddy" podcast in March 2023. articles.title: Vivian Wilson encourages queer people to 'disobey' as midterms approach
articles.summary: The famous transgender model is tired of her community 'being employed as the scapegoat to make people forget about the economy, the Iran war, and the Epstei...
articles.body:
Vivian Jenna Wilson knows what's at stake for the LGBTQ+ community. With the fast-approaching midterms, the famous transgender model is using her platform to showcase her unapologetic queerness at a pivotal moment in history.

Wilson has teamed up with Desigual on their empowering new campaign, Born to Disobey , which encourages queer people to claim their freedom and question society's traditional rules. In the viral campaign photos, she even takes a stand against the rise of AI and technology by playfully mocking a robot.

" It was such a great time participating in this campaign. The title is very charming and somewhat of an oxymoron, but systems are not fought with campaigns. They are fought with protests, activists, and societal political movements demanding sweeping changes. The midterms are coming up and we are being employed as the scapegoat to make people forget about the economy, the Iran war, and the Epstein files," Wilson tells Out .

As LGBTQ+ equality remains a hot-button topic in today's hostile political climate, Wilson is reminding her queer peers to fight back and make their voices heard at the polls this November.

"The importance of queer people building community and support networks in this time cannot be understated. With the government attempting to ban gender affirming care for trans people through an already broken and corrupt healthcare system, the repealment of anti-discrimination laws, and the demonization of queer people, we need to be there for each other right now."

Wilson understands that the LGBTQ+ community has fought for basic rights for decades, but she argues now is not the time for complacency when a potential blue wave could spark crucial progress.

"Look forward to conservatives shouting incessantly about us like kids whose ball went over the fence. Unfortunately, because they are completely incompetent, they have decided to try and distract everyone with how ookity-spookity trans people are."

While the transgender model is proactively creating opportunities and safe spaces for her chosen family, Wilson also reminds everyone to lean on one another through every major milestone. She also hopes to see every queer person expressing themselves as freely as they'd like.

"Many of us, including myself, end up having most of our typical teenage experiences in early adulthood. I think there's a specific beauty in that. Fashion has helped me figure out who I am, and made me more confident in my aesthetic and how I'm facing the world. To be honest, the people I met in fashion have likely had more of an impact on me than fashion itself. You are not alone. Find queer community however you can will always be my advice. Just be careful, safety should always be your priority."

The model was found dead in her home in India on May 12

Twisha Sharma, a 33-year-old model, was found dead just months after her wedding. Now, her husband and mother-in-law have been charged in connection with her death.

Sharma's husband Samarth Singh and mother-in-law Giribala Singh have been charged with abetment to suicide and cruelty, according to a document from The Central Bureau of Investigation reviewed by the BBC .

Sharma was discovered dead outside her home on May 12 in Bhopal, India, per Jam Press.

She married Samarth in December 2025 after they met on a dating app.

The CBI said its investigation found that Samarth, a lawyer, subjected Sharma to mental cruelty and used derogatory language toward her. Giribala, a retired judge, would occasionally "instigate her son to commit mental cruelty on Twisha," the document stated, per the BBC.

"Due to continuous mental cruelty at the hands of both the accused, she was left with no option but to end her life," the CBI said.

Samarth and Giribala have denied the allegations. They are currently being held in jail, per the BBC.

Giribala has alleged that Twisha was struggling with drug addiction.

The former beauty queen's family claim that she was tortured by the suspects over dowry demands, reported the BBC. The family also said there was conflict between the three after Sharma became pregnant in April.

Giribala has denied the claim, stating that Sharma wanted the abortion.

A second autopsy was requested after Sharma's family alleged foul play, per the Independent . The autopsy found that Sharma died by suicide and there were no injuries to suggest assault or struggle.

articles.title: Steve Ballmer got suspended by the NBA because of a podcast and a jumbotron corruption scandal
articles.summary: The NBA’s investigation into Steve Ballmer and the Clippers reveals arrangements with Daktronics, Aspiration, Boingo, and others to pay Kawhi Leonard extra.
articles.body: Last September, Steve Ballmer insisted in an ESPN interview that the Clippers weren’t involved in a shady-looking $28 million endorsement deal for his star player, Kawhi Leonard, that involved no actual endorsing. Now, the former Microsoft CEO has been suspended by the NBA for a year, while the league says his team will forfeit five future draft picks and pay a $30 million fine, among other penalties. A year later, an NBA-commissioned 35-page report by Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is basically calling him a liar, saying those claims were “inaccurate (at best) with respect to Mr. Ballmer” and “clearly false” when it came to Clippers president of business operations Gillian Zucker, who is also suspended for a year. Leonard has accepted the punishment of a $700,000 fine and a ban for his business manager. Now the Clippers are writing angry letters to the NBA, claiming a biased investigation spurred by “a podcaster’s baseless claims” has cost Ballmer $50 million for lawyers, cost more for his reputation, and upset partners like Daktronics, the company that built a massive 4K scoreboard for the team’s new arena, with its many, many bathrooms. That unnamed podcast, of course, is Pablo Torre Finds Out, which is cited at the beginning of the document for kicking this whole thing off one year ago today. [Media: The episode made largely unknown fintech startup / green bank / massive fraud Aspiration a household name, and launched a series by the former ESPN reporter and his team. Now the league’s report is filling out the role partners like Daktronics played in getting Leonard money above and beyond the NBA’s mandated salary cap and how it was tied to that massive scoreboard. > In the spring of 2020, and in response to a request-for-proposal process initiated by the Clippers, Daktronics began to compete to obtain a lucrative contract to supply digital scoreboard and signage technology at the Intuit Dome. In May 2020, the Clippers informed Daktronics that it was the team’s preferred provider for this project, but that the team wanted to agree on a “spend back” arrangement whereby Daktronics would provide some amount of business back to the Clippers—which Daktronics told investigators is not uncommon in its industry. Ms. Zucker thereafter suggested to a Daktronics senior executive that this “spend back” could be accomplished through an endorsement agreement between Daktronics and Mr. Leonard. The report says that an unnamed Clippers executive told Daktronics exactly how much to pay Leonard ($3 million for two years), and eventually told the company in 2021 “that, because the team had decided to increase the amount it would spend on the scoreboard, Daktronics should correspondingly increase the amount it would pay to Mr. Leonard.” As we mentioned at the time, costs for the eventual Intuit Dome had reportedly ballooned to over $2 billion, including the Daktronics-built “Halo Board,” a double-sided 44,000-square-foot wraparound 4K screen with a price said to be over $100 million. Said the now-suspended executive Zucker when it was announced, “We are excited to partner with Daktronics, an innovator in video displays, to develop a Halo Board that will create one of the most intense live experiences in sports.” Daktronics, according to the investigators, along with now-incarcerated Aspiration cofounder Joe Sanberg and what remains of the company in bankruptcy proceedings, cooperated with the investigation. However, there are two other Clippers-affiliated companies apparently involved in paying Leonard an extra $18 million, including Lockton Insurance, which refused to cooperate, and Boingo Wireless, which should probably add an anti-snitching policy to its terms of service. According to investigators, Boingo “purported initially to cooperate, but then supplied information that was inconsistent or not credible to investigators and ultimately refused to cooperate further.” Aspiration, which kicked the whole thing off and had advertised itself as “Wall Street greed’s worst nightmare,” turned into just that for investors including Ballmer, as reported sham endorsement deals by cofounder Joe Sanberg were part of a scheme to create fake revenue. He would eventually be sentenced to 14 years in prison for costing investors $248 million. While the league’s punishment for Ballmer and the Clippers largely ignores the details of Aspiration’s deal and Ballmer’s $50 million investment, the report now includes a note that at the time, Sanberg explained the curious arrangement to other executives differently, emailing an employee to say that “[the Forum is] going to purchase $7mm of reforestation capacity each year from Aspiration to make the ticket experience carbon neutral and potentially carbon negative. To be clear, the $7mm figure per year is set so what’s variable is how they choose to use it.” That figure matched Leonard’s endorsement payments. Other explanations were even more clear about the connection to Kawhi Leonard: > When these concerns were conveyed to Mr. Sanberg, he told the Aspiration executives that “the Clippers are asking us to do this with Kawhi Leonard” and that the team would provide additional business back to Aspiration to help offset the financial impact on Aspiration. In an email exchange among Aspiration’s CEO, CFO, and general counsel, one wrote, “[Mr. Sanberg said] that the Clippers are promising to increase the amount they pay us per quarter in line with what we pay this guy [i.e., Mr. Leonard].” Another responded: “Thanks for verifying. . . . We should be fine if it’s cashflow neutral.” One Clippers executive called its stadium deals with Aspiration “super shady” and full of red flags in text messages to the team’s CFO, and the investigation revealed that while Ballmer and Zucker claimed the $7 million annual arrangement was the result of a study done by a team consultant, the consultant disagreed. > No Clippers witness could provide a credible alternative explanation for the initial appearance of the $7 million annual payment from the team to Aspiration in the Forum Agreement. Mr. Ballmer and Ms. Zucker both claimed that it was based on a study done by a team consultant who had determined that the Forum needed $28 million to offset its carbon emissions and that the team would pay Aspiration for these offsets over four years. But investigators spoke directly with this consultant, who said that the Clippers had given him a $28 million budget with which to address the Forum’s emissions—not the other way around. After untold hours of podcasts (including Torre’s triumphant two-hour live reaction to the report), repeated blanket Clippers denials, and at least one fraud conviction, the investigation still isn’t over. The investigators are looking into a claim that “the consulting agreement one company signed with the Clippers was in fact a ruse, designed and intended to be a vehicle for the team to provide the company with funds to be paid to Mr. Leonard.” Ballmer’s lawyers say they are “exploring every legal remedy to address this gross injustice,” but if I were on the investigation I’d just want to know which one is a bigger regret — giving up 10 draft picks and the rights to a future two-time MVP in the Shai Gilgeous-Alexander trade or launching Windows Vista?
